description:
No. 95 is the Georgian green that people actually remember. It was very popular in Central Asia, and its reputation rests on one thing: a pronounced, tart astringency.

It was a step on the numbered Soviet Georgian scale, where quality rose with the number and topped out at No. 125 before Bouquet and Extra. A Georgian account goes further and names No. 95 among the best green teas of the range.

How it was made is poorly recorded, so the taste is the main thing to go on. If you want the grip it was loved for, do not baby it; if it gets too sharp, shorten the steep before lowering the leaf.

Treat any modern packet with the number as a tribute until proven otherwise, and ask who made it and when.
history:
The tea is documented from the Soviet period, as part of Georgia's numbered green grades. It was especially popular in Central Asia.

Little is documented about its origin as a grade or how long the original standard lasted.
